passages.text: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
passages.sermon:
God appoints all governing authorities.
God gives all authority.
No authority exists unless God gives it.
God appoints every king and every queen.
God appoints every president and governor.
God appoints every judge and those who create laws.
God appoints every police officer and government official.
All existing authorities have been established by God.
Every person must submit to the governing authorities.
However if any government official commands or asks us to sin, then we must obey God and not men.
passages.original: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ Θεοῦ αἱ δὲ οὖσαι ὑπὸ Θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν

passages.text: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
passages.sermon:
God appoints all authority.
Whoever resists the authority opposes what God has established.
If we oppose God’s order then we will bring judgment on ourselves.
passages.original: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται

passages.text: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
passages.sermon:
Rulers have authority over people.
God has appointed these rulers.
Rulers do not cause fear for those who do good.
Rulers cause fear for those who do evil.
If you want to live without fear of authority, then do what is good.
If you do what is good, then the authority will praise you.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κακῷ θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς

passages.text: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.
passages.sermon:
The ruler is God’s servant.
God appoints the ruler to do good for us.
If we do wrong, we should be afraid.
The ruler does not carry the sword for no reason.
The ruler has the authority from God to kill with the sword or some other way.
The ruler has the authority from God to punish with weapons.
The ruler is God’s servant.
He punishes those who do wrong.
passages.original: Θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς φοβοῦ οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ Θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι

passages.text: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.
passages.sermon:
God appoints rulers as authorities.
These rulers have power over people.
We must submit to these authorities.
We should not submit just to avoid punishment.
We should also submit because our conscience tells us to do what is right.
passages.original: Διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν

passages.text: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
passages.sermon:
The authorities serve God.
The authorities devote themselves to their work of governing people.
This is why we pay taxes.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε λειτουργοὶ γὰρ Θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες

passages.text: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
passages.sermon:
God commands us to pay what we owe to everyone.
We must give taxes to those who collect taxes.
We must give revenue to those who collect revenue.
We must give respect to those who deserve respect.
We must give honor to those who deserve honor.
passages.original: ἀπόδοτε πᾶσιν τὰς ὀφειλάς τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν

passages.text: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
passages.sermon:
Do not owe anything to anyone.
If you owe something, only owe this: love one another.
If you love your neighbor, you fulfill the law.
passages.original: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε εἰ μὴ τὸ ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν

passages.text: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
passages.sermon:
God gave commandments.
God says, “Do not commit adultery.”
God says, “Do not murder.”
God says, “Do not steal.”
God says, “Do not covet.”
God gave other commandments too.
All these commandments can be summarized.
God sums up all the commandments in one commandment.
Here is the commandment that summarizes the others: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
passages.original: τὸ γάρ Οὐ μοιχεύσεις Οὐ φονεύσεις Οὐ κλέψεις Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται ἐν τῷ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν

passages.text: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
passages.sermon:
Love does not harm its neighbor.
Love never does evil to another person.
Love fulfills the law completely.
Love is the full measure of what the law requires.
passages.original: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη

passages.text: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
passages.sermon:
Paul tells us to understand the present time.
The hour has come.
Now is the hour for us to wake up from our sleep.
Our salvation is closer now than when we first believed.
passages.original: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν ὅτι ὥρα ἤδη ὑμᾶς ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν

passages.text: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
passages.sermon:
As an analogy, the night is almost finished.
This world with its evil is almost finished because the return of Jesus is near.
And, as an analogy, the day is very close now.
Jesus ruling in the kingdom that will be full of the light of the glory of God is near.
Let us stop doing the works of darkness.
Let us put on the armor of light.
passages.original: ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν ἀποθώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους ἐνδυσώμεθα δὲ τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτός

passages.text: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
passages.sermon:
When it has been daytime, many people have waited until night to commit sin because they believe no one will see them in the dark or hear them because they're sleeping.
Whereas when it's daytime and everyone can hear and see, then they behave properly.
Let us behave properly.
Let us behave as people do in the daytime.
Let us not join in wild parties.
Let us not get drunk.
Let us not take part in sexual immorality.
Let us not do shameful things to satisfy sinful pleasure.
Let us not argue with each other.
Let us not be jealous of one another.
passages.original: ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν μὴ κώμοις καὶ μέθαις μὴ κοίταις καὶ ἀσελγείαις μὴ ἔριδι καὶ ζήλῳ

passages.text: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
passages.sermon:
Clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ.
Do not make plans to satisfy the desires of your flesh.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς πρόνοιαν μὴ ποιεῖσθε εἰς ἐπιθυμίας
